difficultyRationale: Checks the compile-time exhaustiveness requirement of switch expressions.
prompt: Which statement about a Java 21 `switch` expression is correct?
explanation: A switch expression must be exhaustive: every possible selector value must be handled by a matching label or by a construct the compiler can prove exhaustive.

options.text: It may omit all unmatched values and implicitly return null.
options.explanation: There is no implicit null result for unmatched selector values.
Every switch expression must cover all possible selector values.

options.text: It must always contain a default label, even when enum cases are exhaustive.
options.explanation: A default label is not mandatory when exhaustiveness can be proven another way.

options.text: Only integer selectors can be used in switch expressions.
options.explanation: Other supported selector types include enum, String, and reference types with pattern matching.
